Objectives.text: The objective of the Group is the advancement of public education through the promotion of interdisciplinary involvement in the collection, analysis and dissemination of data relating to the history, geography and archaeology of medieval settlements and their associated landscapes.

Trustees’ Addresses.text: Dr R J Silvester (President), Braich-uchaf, Cil Road, Meifod, Powys SY22 6YA Dr J Naylor (Secretary), Ashmolean Museum, Beaumont Street, Oxford, OX1 2PH Dr R E Glasscock (Treasurer), St John’s College, Cambridge CB2 1TP Dr S C Turner (Editor), School of History, Classics and Archaeology, Newcastle University NE1 7RU

Review of activity during the year.text: The Group’s activities (policy making, conferences and publication) have continued as before. The range of interests and issues i reflected in the content of the accompanying journal (Medieval Settlement Research 32) covering the year 2017.

Result of the year.text: There was a surplus of income over expenditure of £739 (deficit of £2,102 in 2015–16).

Reserves policy.text: The trustees’ policy is to maintain reserves at a level to enable long term and other research projects to be sustained in the foreseeable future.

Grant making policy.text: The charity makes grants towards research projects and to other bodies involved in similar areas of education and research in respect of medieval settlement.

Investments policy.text: The charity’s funds are invested in National Savings and a bank bond, deposits that are regarded as a safe liquid investment with an adequate return, and suitable for a small charity.

Risk policy.text: The trustees have reviewed the major risks facing the charity and presently conclude that no specific action is required.

INDEPENDENT EXAMINER’S REPORT TO THE TRU.text: I report on the accounts for the year ended 31 January 2017 which are set out on the following page.

Respective responsibilities of Trustees.text: The charity’s trustees are responsible for the preparation of the account. The charity’s trustees consider that an audit is not required for this year under Section 43(2) of the Charities Act 1993 (the Act) and that an independent examination is needed.

Basis of independent examiner’s report.text: My examination was carried out in accordance with the General Directions given by the Charity Commissioners. An examination includes a review of the accounting records kept by the charity and comparison of the accounts presented with those records. It also includes consideration of any unusual items or disclosures in the accounts, and seeking explanations from the trustees concerning any such matters. The procedures undertaken do not provide all the evidence that would be required in an audit, and consequently I do not express an audit opinion on the accounts.

In connection with my examination, no matter has come to my attention: (1) which gives me reasonable cause to believe that in any material respect the requirements (2) to which, in my opinion, attention should be drawn in order to enable a proper understanding of the accounts to be reached.
Kate Harvey FCA Head of Finance St John’s College Cambridge CB2 1TP 12 April 2017
